title: Sweet Chestnut: Ancient Chestnuts You Can Visit
meta_description: In January 1949 a runaway bus above Trento was stopped by a chestnut tree. Six old sweet chestnuts mapped, the oldest around 600 years.
intro: In January 1949 a runaway bus above Trento was stopped by a chestnut tree, and local accounts still argue about which one. Sweet chestnut collects that kind of story because it stays around long enough: the one in Ashton Park in Bristol is about 600 years old, and the three at Arnhem, known locally as Hans, Gretel and the Witch, have been standing roughly 370. The trunk gives the age away better than any plaque, because as a chestnut ages its bark starts to spiral around the stem, and on the oldest trees the whole trunk looks wrung out like a towel. Charles II is behind the Greenwich Park tree, one of the chestnuts planted for the formal avenues he ordered cut through the park after taking the throne in 1660. Six are mapped, including the oldest tree in Edinburgh's Botanics, which was growing there before the garden arrived.
